title: Quant Tuning Primer for Real-time Hybrid Workloads
author: Mariana Soto
body:
Summary

This primer describes a reproducible, safety-first process for producing and validating quantization profiles targeted specifically at hybrid workloads: low-latency real-time inference (P99 < 120 ms) mixed with periodic high-throughput batch jobs. It consolidates benchmarking matrices, tuning recipes, telemetry gates, and rollback guidance so ML engineers and SREs can reliably deploy quantized model artifacts to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments.

When to use this document

- You are migrating a float32 or bf16 model to int8/4/LLM quantized formats to reduce per-token cost while maintaining real-time latency SLOs.
- The application mixes conversational traffic (short context, tight tail latency requirements) and scheduled bulk jobs (long context, high throughput).
- You need a standardized validation matrix for coherence, KV-cache fidelity, and tail latency.

Key objectives

1) Maintain conversational P99 latency <= 120 ms on target hardware tier for <= 256-token requests.
2) Ensure response coherence degradation (semantic similarity) < 2.5% on guarded prompt-slices.
3) Preserve KV-cache correctness across pitch-and-roll warmups for multi-turn flows.

Terminology

- Hybrid workload: stream of low-latency requests + periodic high-throughput batches.
- Profile: named quantization configuration (e.g., q8_hybrid_lowlat).
- Safe gate: automated threshold that prevents rollout if metric regressions exceed threshold.

Prerequisites

- Baseline float runbook and golden prompt set (see: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/production-prompt-catalog-and-stress-bench-2025).
- Access to telemetry: token-level latency, coherence scores, KV cache hit/miss, and per-request seed.
- Target hardware specification (GPU type, SLO targets) and an ephemeral Dedicated instance for profiling.

Benchmark matrix (example)

Columns: Profile | Mean Tokens/sec (batch) | P50 Latency (short) | P99 Latency (short) | Coherence Δ (anchor) | KV-cache drift
- q_fp32_baseline | 120 | 18 ms | 90 ms | 0.0% | 0%
- q8_hybrid_lowlat | 230 | 20 ms | 110 ms | +0.9% | 0.7%
- q4_ultra_compress | 480 | 28 ms | 210 ms | +3.8% | 2.5%

Interpretation guidance

- Profiles that show Coherence Δ > 2.5% or KV-cache drift > 1.0% should not be promoted for low-latency routes.
- A profile with P99 > 150 ms requires either changing batching policy (lower batch latency SLA) or disabling that profile on real-time routes.

Tuning procedure (ordered checklist)

1) Baseline capture
   - Run float baseline over a stratified probe set: short-turn chat (70%), medium-turn assistant (20%), long context batch (10%).
   - Capture token-level traces, KV hit/miss, and seed.

2) Candidate profile generation
   - Produce candidate quant profiles using the quant builder. Example command:

     ./tools/quant-builder --model checkpoints/mymodel/bf16 --out profiles/q8_hybrid_lowlat --mode per-channel --calib-samples 2048

   - Save profile metadata: model_hash, quant_seed, kernel_variant.

3) Microbenchmarks (latency and throughput)
   - Use the perf harness to measure short-context tail latency and batch throughput. Example YAML config:

     workload:
       name: hybrid-short-and-batch
       mixes:
         - type: short_chat
           p99_target_ms: 120
           weight: 0.7
         - type: batch_long
           batch_size: 64
           weight: 0.3

   - Capture P50/P95/P99 and mean tokens/sec.

4) Fidelity probes (coherence / semantic tests)
   - Run guarded prompt-slices (n=1500) and compute semantic similarity against baseline using the designated embedder and calibrated threshold.
   - Record confusion types (hallucination, truncated token dropout, verbatim repeat).

5) KV-cache integrity test
   - Run warmup sequences (n=200) with interleaved multi-turn reads/writes; compare generated token prefixes post-warmup between baseline and quantized model. Log drift score.

6) Combined stress test
   - Simulate production multiplexing: 5000 short requests/min + hourly batch job. Run for 2 hours and observe tail latency spikes and p50 shifts.

7) Failure mode classification and safe gates
   - If any of the following triggers, block rollout to real-time route by the CD pipeline:
     a) Coherence Δ > 2.5% on high-priority slices.
     b) KV-cache drift > 1% on multi-turn sequences.
     c) P99 increase > 30 ms relative to baseline.

Profile promotion rules

- Canary: promote to 1% of traffic on a subset of tenants for 24h with continuous monitoring. If safe gates hold for 24h, proceed to 25% for 48h.
- Full: promote gradually to 100% over 7 days with automated rollback triggers.

Example quant profile YAML (explainable fields)

profile_name: q8_hybrid_lowlat
backend: tensor-kernels-v2
precision: int8
per_channel: true
calibration_samples: 2048
optimize_attention_kv: true
kv_cache_mode: consistent
kernel_variant: split-fused-attn
notes: "Tuned for low-latency conversational route; retains per-channel scales for attention layers"

Telemetry and alerts (SRE playbook hooks)

- Essential metrics to stream to Console: quant_profile, model_version, route, p50/p95/p99, coherence_delta_slice_major, kv_cache_drift_pct, error_rate_%
- Alert thresholds:
  - High severity: coherence_delta_slice_major > 3.0% for 30m or p99 > 200 ms for 10m.
  - Medium severity: kv_cache_drift_pct > 1.5% for 1h.

Rollback recipe (fast path)

1) Automated circuit-breaker sees a gating violation and marks rollout as failed.
2) CD triggers immediate traffic shift back to baseline profile (0% quant profile) using weighted routing. Expected propagation: 30s–120s.
3) Trigger an eval-oncall runbook (see eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging-2026) and capture artifacts.

Ownership and responsibilities

- Model owner: ensures candidate profiles and annotations are uploaded.
- Performance lead (SRE): authorizes hardware tier for profiling and declares acceptable P99.
- Eval steward: validates guarded slices, runs coherence scoring, and signs off promotion.

Appendix A — Quick checklist for PR reviewers

- [ ] Baseline traces attached and hash-verified.
- [ ] Probe set results present (short/medium/long).
- [ ] KV-cache drift report included.
- [ ] Canary plan with ownership and rollback steps documented.

Appendix B — Useful CLI snippets

- Build candidate: ./tools/quant-builder --model <path> --out <profile> --mode per-tensor --calib-samples 1024
- Run perf harness: ./harness/perf --config configs/hybrid-short-batch.yaml --profile profiles/q8_hybrid_lowlat
- Compute coherence: python tools/coherence_score.py --baseline traces/baseline.json --compare traces/q8_run.json --slices guarded-list.csv

Appendix C — Example failure taxonomy (triage labels)

- latency_degradation: tail-latency regressions on short requests.
- kv_inconsistency: multi-turn divergence due to cache mismatch.
- semantic_shift: abrupt meaning changes or hallucinations.
- tokenization_loss: token-level truncation or broken decoding.
